slide-fx · 3D layer

3D Engineering
Slides

The same deck model, rendered in WebGL. Mechanisms, assemblies, and surfaces — with three.js or Babylon.js, chosen per slide.

01 · Why 3D

Some things only make sense in space.

Linkages that move out of plane, assemblies that stack, kinematics with a wrist, surfaces over a domain. This is one scene — exploded sensor pod — driven by the same build() + per-frame updater model as the 2D engine.

02 · Kinematics

A 3-DOF arm solving IK to a moving target.

Base yaw plus a two-link planar solve in the rotated plane — the same math you would put on a slide as an equation, shown as motion.

03 · Two engines, one scene

The identical preset, rendered by three.js and Babylon.js.

three.js  ·  data-lib="three"
Babylon.js  ·  data-lib="babylon"

Presets are written once against a small common API (groups, meshes, lines, camera, per-frame updates). Swap the backend by changing one attribute.

04 · Assemblies

Exploded views you can narrate.

Parts separate, hold, and re-seat on a timeline — driven here by a phase variable rather than a canned animation.

05 · Math & data

Surfaces, fields, and response shapes.

z = f(x, y) sampled into an adaptive wireframe — saddle by default; set fn to gauss or ripple per slide.

06 · How it works

One attribute picks the engine.

<!-- a slide chooses its renderer --> <div class="fx" data-fx="arm3d" data-lib="three"></div> <div class="fx" data-fx="arm3d" data-lib="babylon"></div> // presets are backend-agnostic — one body of code, both engines var s = SlideFX.scene3d(canvas, { lib: 'babylon' }); s.build(function (sc, g) { var base = g.group(); var arm = g.box(0.42, 2.0, 0.34, { color: SlideFX.C3.accent, parent: base }); g.grid(12, 12); g.axes(2.2); g.camera({ pos:[7,4.6,7], target:[0,1.5,0] }); sc.update(function (dt, t) { base.ry += dt * 0.6; arm.rz = -t; }); });

07 · Takeaway

Pick the renderer per slide, not per deck.

Most slides need nothing but text and a static diagram. When a slide is about something spatial — a mechanism, an assembly stack, a surface — reach for 3D, and pick three.js when you want the smaller, lighter embed, or Babylon.js when you want its batteries-included engine. The deck stays one file either way.
